assumptions: The NL states that there are twelve finite states but does not provide formal state names; the model uses descriptive synthesized state names for the twelve logical dispatch cases.
The input bundle has no SpecJson state/transition list, so the guard partition is an initial condition-classification abstraction rather than a verified reproduction of an upstream formal EMS table.
Battery suitability is approximated with SoC >= 0.2 for discharge and SoC < 0.2 for low-SoC charging branches because only the high charge threshold 0.95 was explicitly stated.

eng3_Pmax is treated as the LNG engine capacity bound, Pd1max and Pd2max as DG1 and DG2 capacity bounds, and Pbat_Pmax as an admitted battery discharge capacity variable required to express battery-limited dispatch.
Cut-in and cut-out load commands are represented as aggregate load commands because the NL does not list individual load classes.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, EMS serves demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Dispatch priority uses batteries when suitable and LNG before diesel units.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
DG1/DG2 only as last priority after RES, batteries, and LNG.

Because the NL says the overload completion state is illegal and shall never occur in practice, the state now issues fail-safe load cut-out commands rather than treating the impossible overload as normal service.
No required states, variables, forced dispatch classification transitions, or non-overload dispatch equations were removed or broadened.

accepted_edit_intent: Clamp OverloadCompletionIllegal battery discharge to Pbat_Pmax using pyfcstm action-block conditional syntax.

decisions.rationale: Accepted the model-review hard block. evidence.summary: The NL requires twelve dispatch states including an illegal overload-completion state, all thermal units active under extreme overload, battery discharge/charging outputs, spare power, and cut-in/cut-out commands. The candidate preserves all twelve states, all declared input/output variables, and all forced classification guards, including OverloadCompletionIllegal.

The sole SL-7 hard-block request was unsafe_recovery: the old OverloadCompletionIllegal branch commanded Pbat_dis as the full residual deficit, which could exceed Pbat_Pmax, and kept loads cut in. SL-9 accepted that request and proposed the smallest targeted repair: clamp Pbat_dis to Pbat_Pmax and issue load cut-out in the illegal state while preserving all thermal requests.

The DSL diff matches the accepted repair intent and is localized to OverloadCompletionIllegal.enter: Plng_req, Pd1_req, and Pd2_req still request eng3_Pmax, Pd1max, and Pd2max; Pbat_dis is first computed as the residual lack and then capped if greater than Pbat_Pmax; cut_in_loads/cut_out_loads are changed from 1/0 to 0/1. No non-overload dispatch equations or guards were changed.

Local deterministic simulation passed 14 of 15 scenarios. The only failing scenario is overload_completion_illegal_extreme_demand, where the oracle expected the old unsafe outputs Pbat_dis=220.0 with Pbat_Pmax=40.0 and loads kept cut in. The candidate instead produced Pbat_dis=40.0 and cut_out_loads=1, which directly addresses the hard-blocked unsafe behavior rather than creating an NL-fidelity regression.

Those expected values are precisely the unsafe old behavior cited by the SL-7 hard block: battery discharge beyond Pbat_Pmax and normal load service in an illegal overload branch.

The NL says the overload completion state is illegal and shall never occur in practice. The FixLog and SL-9 decision interpret this required illegal branch as fail-safe/diagnostic rather than a normal dispatch state. Clamping battery discharge to Pbat_Pmax respects the modeled battery capacity bound while still activating all thermal units and applying maximum available battery discharge; cutting out loads gives clear fail-safe semantics for an impossible overload condition.

Because the only local failure is the intentionally changed unsafe overload oracle and all other scenarios, required states, guards, variables, and non-overload dispatch actions remain preserved, the local regression is not treated as a real scenario or NL-fidelity regression for the next top-down revalidation pass.

Those expected values are precisely the unsafe old behavior cited by the SL-7 hard block: battery discharge beyond Pbat_Pmax and normal load service in an illegal overload branch.

The NL says the overload completion state is illegal and shall never occur in practice. The FixLog and SL-9 decision interpret this required illegal branch as fail-safe/diagnostic rather than a normal dispatch state. Clamping battery discharge to Pbat_Pmax respects the modeled battery capacity bound while still activating all thermal units and applying maximum available battery discharge; cutting out loads gives clear fail-safe semantics for an impossible overload condition.

Because the only local failure is the intentionally changed unsafe overload oracle and all other scenarios, required states, guards, variables, and non-overload dispatch actions remain preserved, the local regression is not treated as a real scenario or NL-fidelity regression for the next top-down revalidation pass.

decisions.rationale: Accepted. Although earlier iterations rejected the same local scenario as stale, the current bundle contains a blocking non-weak simulation oracle plus grounding/root-cause evidence that the prior clamp/load-shedding behavior was not reconciled with the NL. The repair_brief for overload_completion_illegal_extreme_demand expects state LNGShipEMS.OverloadCompletionIllegal with all thermal units active, Pbat_dis equal to the full remaining lack, and loads kept cut in. The NL says that in this illegal extreme-demand case the EMS activates all thermal generating units and covers the lack by battery discharge; it does not state that battery discharge is capped by Pbat_Pmax or that loads are shed in this state. The smallest safe edit is therefore confined to OverloadCompletionIllegal.enter.

diff_summary.summary: Only OverloadCompletionIllegal.enter changed: removed the Pbat_dis > Pbat_Pmax clamp and changed load commands from cut_out to cut_in. No state names, guards, declarations, or other dispatch-state actions were changed.

repair_rationale: Fixed scenario overload_completion_illegal_extreme_demand, step all_thermal_and_battery_lack: expected_state and actual_state already matched LNGShipEMS.OverloadCompletionIllegal, so no state/guard restructure was needed.

For the failing vars, expected Pbat_dis=220.0 while actual was 40.0 because OverloadCompletionIllegal clamped Pbat_dis to Pbat_Pmax. The edit removes that clamp so Pbat_dis is the remaining lack PL - Ppv - Pw - eng3_Pmax - Pd1max - Pd2max, giving 400 - 0 - 0 - 50 - 60 - 70 = 220.

For the failing load command vars, expected cut_in_loads=1 and cut_out_loads=0 while actual was cut_in_loads=0 and cut_out_loads=1. The edit keeps loads cut in for the illegal completion case, matching the oracle and the NL statement that the EMS covers the lack by battery discharge after activating all thermal units.

All twelve required states, all required variables, aggregate cut-in/cut-out command variables, and the zero-load classification transition are preserved. Passing scenarios for the other dispatch states are not changed because the edit is limited to OverloadCompletionIllegal.enter.
